content.value_statement: Inconsistent reviews miss defects and create unclear feedback. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured checklist for secure and maintainable pull request reviews.
actual_capabilities: Classifies review feedback with critical, high, medium, and low severity levels.
Checks pull requests for correctness, security, TypeScript quality, tests, performance, and maintainability.
Provides review templates for security, TypeScript, performance, and code quality findings.
Highlights common code smells such as long functions, deep nesting, magic numbers, and dead code.
Guides reviewers through pre-review, security review, detailed review, feedback, and verdict steps.
Links review decisions to supporting checklists for security, performance, and maintainability.
limitations: It is a review framework, not an automated scanner or test runner.
It references related skills that may not be installed in every environment.
It focuses on TypeScript, Next.js, Drizzle, Zod, and similar web application patterns.
It cannot confirm runtime behavior without access to the target repository and test results.

use_cases.title: Standardize Pull Request Reviews
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to keep reviewer feedback consistent across correctness, security, tests, performance, and maintainability.

use_cases.title: Train New Reviewers
use_cases.description: Give new engineers concrete severity levels, examples, and feedback templates for their first code reviews.

use_cases.title: Audit Risky Application Changes
use_cases.description: Apply extra scrutiny to authentication, API, database, and data handling changes before merge.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Pull Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a focused change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-review-standards skill to review this pull request. Focus on correctness, tests, security, and clear severity labels.

prompt_templates.title: Check TypeScript and Maintainability
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for code quality and type safety.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript change with the code-review-standards checklist. Flag any type safety, naming, duplication, dead code, or error handling issues.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Security and Performance Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of application code with user data or database access.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use code-review-standards to review this auth, API, or data change. Prioritize security, authorization, validation, query efficiency, caching, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Merge Readiness Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the full code-review-standards process. Return a severity-grouped review, required fixes, optional suggestions, and a merge verdict.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds a login route with weak validation and missing error tests.
output: Critical issue: validate login input before authentication logic runs.
High issue: add tests for invalid email, wrong password, and expired token cases.
Verdict: request changes until security and coverage gaps are fixed.

output_examples.input: A service change adds several database queries inside a loop.
output: High issue: replace repeated per-row queries with a joined or batched query.
Medium issue: add a benchmark or query timing note for the changed path.
Verdict: request changes if the path handles large datasets.

output_examples.input: A utility module includes unclear names, duplicated validation, and no documented edge case tests.
output: Medium issue: extract shared validation so create and update paths use one rule set.
Low issue: rename short variables to describe the business meaning.
Verdict: comment or request changes based on the size of the affected surface.

best_practices: Start every review by identifying high-risk areas such as authentication, payments, and data handling.
Group findings by severity so required fixes are easy to separate from suggestions.
Tie each issue to a concrete file, risk, and suggested fix.
anti_patterns: Do not approve changes with unresolved critical security or data loss risks.
Do not give vague feedback without a location, impact, or actionable fix.
Do not focus only on style while ignoring tests, validation, authorization, and performance.

faq.question: Does this skill run code or tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides review criteria and templates. The reviewer must run tests or tools separately when needed.

faq.question: Which languages does it fit best?
faq.answer: It is strongest for TypeScript and modern web applications, especially Next.js, Drizzle, Zod, and React patterns.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify common issues, but high-risk security changes still need specialist review.

faq.question: How should severity labels be used?
faq.answer: Critical and high findings should block merge. Medium and low findings can guide follow-up work or comments.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should reviewers provide as input?
faq.answer: Provide the diff, relevant files, test results, and any product context needed to judge risk and intent.
